title: The Perfect Active
subtitle: λέλυκα — the state resulting from completed action.
objectives: Form and conjugate the perfect active indicative of any ω-verb.
Understand the perfect as expressing the state resulting from completed action.
Recognize reduplication as the marker of the perfect.
Distinguish perfect from aorist by meaning.

sections.heading: The perfect tense
sections.body:
The perfect expresses the state resulting from completed action. λέλυκα means 'I have loosed' or 'I am in the state of having loosed'. The perfect emphasizes the present result of a past action, not just the past action itself.

Aorist: ἔλυσα — 'I loosed' (simple past action).
Perfect: λέλυκα — 'I have loosed' (present state resulting from past action).

The perfect is formed with reduplication (repeating the initial consonant with ε: λε-λυ-) and a new set of endings called the perfect active endings.

sections.heading: The perfect active indicative: λέλυκα
sections.body:
singular
  1st   λέλυκα      I have loosed
  2nd   λέλυκας     you have loosed
  3rd   λέλυκε(ν)   he/she/it has loosed

  plural
  1st   λελύκαμεν   we have loosed
  2nd   λελύκατε    you (plural) have loosed
  3rd   λελύκασι(ν) they have loosed

The endings are -α, -ας, -ε(ν), -αμεν, -ατε, -ασι(ν). The reduplication is λε- (the initial consonant λ + ε). The stem is λυ- + κ (the κ is called the perfect active marker, though not all verbs have it).

sections.heading: Reduplication patterns
sections.body:
Consonant-initial verbs: repeat the initial consonant + ε.
λύω → λέλυκα
παύω → πέπαυκα
γράφω → γέγραφα

Vowel-initial verbs: lengthen the initial vowel (like the augment).
ἀκούω → ἀκήκοα

Compound verbs: reduplicate after the preposition.
ἀπολύω → ἀπολέλυκα

sections.heading: From Plato
sections.body:
Plato, Apology 20c: οὐδὲν οἶδα.
'I know nothing.' οἶδα is the perfect of a root meaning 'see'; it means 'I have seen' = 'I know'. This is one of the most common perfects in Greek, and it is irregular.

items.prompt: First person singular perfect active of λύω
Third person singular perfect active of λύω
Third person plural perfect active of λύω
What is the marker of the perfect tense?
What is the difference between the aorist and the perfect?
items.answer: Aorist: simple past action. Perfect: present state resulting from past action.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 4.9 introduces the perfect middle and passive. The perfect middle/passive uses the same reduplication as the active, but the endings are stacked directly onto the stem without the κ marker. λέλυμαι means 'I have been loosed' or 'I am in the state of having been loosed'.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate the perfect active of any ω-verb from memory and can distinguish perfect from aorist by meaning.
